en: The Jātaka:
The Collection of Ten,
Chapter on the Four Gates (Catudvāravagga)
15. The Mahāmaṅgala Jātaka:
“What should a man pray for at times of distress?
What knowledge should he seek, or what among the teachings (suta) should he hear?”
“Thus, being a mortal in this world and the world beyond,
how can one act so as to be protected by safety?
“For whom both gods and all ancestors...”
Crawling creatures and all beings as well—
when they are constantly honored with loving-kindness,
that indeed is called safety among beings.”
“He who behaves with humility toward the whole world—
toward women, men, and children alike;
who is patient with harsh words and does not speak disagreeably;”
They say that forbearance is true prosperity:
he who does not despise his companions and friends on account of their craft, lineage, wealth, or birth.
One who possesses wisdom and discernment during times of need,
they say, finds safety among friends.
Indeed, for one whose friends are virtuous—
One who is trustworthy does not deceive;
one who does not betray friends and shares their wealth— this,
they say, is true security among friends.
He whose wife is of equal age, harmonious, devoted,
desirous of the Dhamma, well-born, virtuous,
and faithful— [for him there is no grief].
They say that safety indeed lies within one's own home for him whom the illustrious King, the Lord of Beings,
recognizes for his purity and his prowess.
"Being free from duplicity and having a kindly heart—
this, they say, is safety among kings.
The faithful one gives food and drink;
Garlands, perfumes, and ointments— one who,
with a confident heart, rejoices in these,
is said to find safety in the heavenly realms.
The elders purify themselves by noble conduct;
the virtuous ones, having attained it through even practice,
are sages of great learning and endowed with moral discipline.
They say that safety lies in the midst of Arahants.
These indeed are the states of safety in the world,
praised by the wise and resulting in happiness.
A wise man should cultivate those here in this world,
for there is nothing true in mere auspicious omens.
Thus ends the fifteenth Jātaka, the Mahāmaṅgala-jātaka.
